paper.title_en: Type Ia supernovae alone do not favor dynamical dark energy: An independent Bayesian model comparison across four modern compilations
paper.abstract_en: Recent analyses combining DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements with Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) compilations and cosmic microwave background (CMB) priors have reported a preference, at the <math altimg="si48.svg"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mspace width="0.16em"/><mn>4</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math> level in frequentist terms, for a time-evolving dark-energy equation of state over a cosmological constant. This preference is known to depend on which SN Ia compilation is used, and several recent studies have shown that a proper Bayesian evidence treatment of the joint BAO+CMB+SN fit is considerably less conclusive than the frequentist significance suggests. What has not been directly reported is whether SN Ia data alone - independent of any BAO or CMB information - shows a Bayesian preference for dynamical dark energy in the first place. We address this using an independently implemented (non-CAMB/Cobaya) Bayesian pipeline: from-scratch flat-FLRW distance calculations, an analytically marginalized SN Ia likelihood, and nested-sampling evidence estimation, applied identically to four current SN Ia compilations (Pantheon+, Union3, DES-SN5YR, and its DES-Dovekie recalibration). Our pipeline reproduces the published SN-alone ΛCDM and wCDM constraints of each compilation to within their quoted uncertainties. We find that none of the four compilations, used alone, shows positive Bayesian evidence for either a constant (wCDM) or time-varying (CPL, w0waCDM) dark-energy equation of state relative to ΛCDM; all four log Bayes factors are negative, ranging from <math altimg="si49.svg"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.8</mn></mrow></math> (Pantheon+, CPL, “substantial” evidence against on the Jeffreys scale) to <math altimg="si50.svg"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.15</mn></mrow></math> (DES-SN5YR, CPL, “barely worth mentioning”). DES-SN5YR - the compilation most responsible for the reported joint-fit preference for dynamical dark energy - is consistently the least unfavorable to the extended models among the four, and its DES-Dovekie recalibration shifts the evidence back toward ΛCDM. This indicates that the reported preference for dynamical dark energy originates from the combination of SN data with BAO and CMB information, not from any SN compilation in isolation, and that its compilation-dependence is present already at the SN-only level.
